reference_memory.normal_pattern: The time series exhibits a highly regular, quasi-sinusoidal oscillation with a robust period of ~182 points (consistent with the estimated period). Each cycle consists of a slow, smooth descent from a broad peak (~2.5–4.0 standardized units) to a sharp, narrow trough near −1.0, followed by a rapid, near-linear ascent back to the next peak. The baseline level is stable across cycles, with median values hovering near 0.0–0.2 and MAD ~0.7, indicating consistent dispersion. Amplitude (90th percentile range) varies modestly between 3.9–4.6, but peak height and trough depth are tightly constrained: peaks consistently reach 3.0–4.1, troughs cluster near −1.0 to −0.8, with minimal intra-cycle distortion. Noise is low—roughness metrics (0.030–0.033) confirm smoothness—and curvature is gentle except near troughs, where steepness increases sharply. A very slight positive trend appears in longer windows (slope per point ~0.0002–0.0008), but it is negligible over single cycles. Boundary truncation is present in candidate 0 (only 1 cycle, cut mid-peak), but morphology within full cycles (candidates 1–3) is highly reproducible. Acceptable variation includes minor asymmetry in ascent/descent slopes and ±0.2 shifts in peak timing; deviations such as flattened peaks, double/triple troughs, or excessive high-frequency jitter would be anomalous.
